name: Button
summary: Initiates an action, such as completing a task or submitting information.
jsdoc: Renders a button or a component that looks like a button, an interactive element activated by a user with a mouse, keyboard, finger, voice command, or other assistive technology.
examples:
The default primary action — filled + neutral:
```tsx
<Button appearance="filled" intent="neutral" onClick={handleClick}>
  Click me
</Button>
```

Submit a form — opt in with `type="submit"` (the default `"button"` does not submit):
```tsx
<Button type="submit" appearance="filled" intent="neutral">
  Save
</Button>
```

Pass the icon through `icon`, never as a child:
```tsx
// ❌ <Button appearance="filled" intent="neutral"><PlusIcon />Create endpoint</Button>
<Button appearance="filled" intent="neutral" icon={<PlusIcon />}>
  Create endpoint
</Button>
```

Gate the button on readiness and on a pending action. An explicit `disabled`
wins over `isLoading`, so `disabled` must cover both:
```tsx
<Button
  type="submit"
  appearance="filled"
  intent="neutral"
  isLoading={isPending}
  disabled={!isReady || isPending}
>
  Save
</Button>
```
A button-styled link wraps a plain ``, not `Anchor`: ```tsx ```

Icon-only buttons are not `Button`s — use `IconButton` instead (an icon-only
`Button` has no accessible name and keeps its text-box padding):
```tsx
// ❌ <Button appearance="outlined" intent="neutral" icon={<CopyIcon />} onClick={copyPage} />
<IconButton appearance="outlined" intent="neutral" icon={<CopyIcon />} label="Copy page" onClick={copyPage} />
```
